query: Are (P implies Q) and (NOT P OR Q) logically equivalent?
reasoning:
1. Recall the definition of the material conditional: "P implies Q" is false only when P is true and Q is false; otherwise it is true.
2. Recall the definition of "NOT P OR Q": it is false only when NOT P is false (i.e. P is true) and Q is false; otherwise it is true.
3. Compare the two conditions from step 1 and step 2: both expressions are false exactly when P is true and Q is false, and true in all other cases. Choose whether they match: yes.
